title: Valid Parentheses
summary: Check that every bracket is closed by the same type in the right order. Push opening brackets; on a closing bracket the top of the stack must be its partner. The string is valid only if the stack ends empty.

complexity.note: Best case is an immediate mismatch. The stack can hold n/2 brackets.

intuition: The most recent unclosed bracket must be closed first: last in, first out.
On `)`, `]`, `}`, pop and check it matches.
A closing bracket with an empty stack is invalid.
Leftover openers at the end are invalid too.
pitfalls: Only counting brackets misses order errors like "([)]".
Popping an empty stack throws; check `isEmpty()` first.
Forgetting the final `isEmpty()` check ("((" would pass).

title: Min Stack
summary: Support push, pop, top and getMin in O(1). Keep a second stack where each entry is the minimum of everything at or below that level. Pushing records `min(x, currentMin)`; popping removes both tops together.

complexity.note: Every operation is O(1); the extra stack doubles the space.

intuition: The minimum only changes when you push or pop, so remember it per level.
`mins.peek()` is always the minimum of the whole stack.
Push `min(x, mins.peek())` so both stacks stay the same height.
pitfalls: Storing a single `min` variable fails after popping the minimum.
Only pushing onto `mins` when x is smaller works, but then pops must compare values; duplicates make that fragile.
Using `Integer ==` instead of `.equals` on boxed values above 127.
input: push(-2), push(0), push(-3), getMin(), pop(), top(), getMin()

complexity.note: Each element of nums2 is pushed and popped at most once.

intuition: Keep the stack decreasing from bottom to top.
A new value pops every smaller value; for each, the new value is its next greater.

pitfalls: Values are distinct here; with duplicates you'd store indices, not values.

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
summary: Evaluate an expression written in postfix, like `2 1 + 3 *`. Push numbers; on an operator, pop the right operand, then the left one, apply the operator, and push the result. The last value on the stack is the answer.

complexity.note: Each token is pushed or popped a constant number of times.

intuition: Postfix needs no parentheses: an operator always applies to the two most recent values.
Pop `b` first, then `a`, and compute `a op b`; order matters for `-` and `/`.
Division truncates toward zero, which is exactly what Java's `/` does.
pitfalls: Checking for operators with `token.charAt(0) == '-'` breaks on negative numbers like "-11".

title: Daily Temperatures
summary: For each day, how many days until a warmer one? Keep a stack of day indices with decreasing temperatures. When a warmer day arrives, pop every cooler day: its answer is the distance to today.

complexity.note: Each index is pushed and popped once.

intuition: Store indices, not temperatures, so you can compute the distance.
Days on the stack are still waiting for a warmer day.
`ans[j] = i - j` when day i pops day j.
Days left on the stack at the end keep the default 0.
pitfalls: Popping on `>=` instead of `>`: equal temperatures are not warmer.
Brute force O(n²) times out on 10⁵ days.

title: Asteroid Collision
summary: Positive asteroids move right, negative ones left; when they meet, the smaller explodes (both if equal). Use a stack of survivors: a left-moving asteroid fights right-movers on top of the stack until it dies, they all die, or no right-mover is left.

complexity.note: Each asteroid is pushed and popped at most once.

intuition: Only a right-mover (top, positive) followed by a left-mover (current, negative) can collide.
While the top is smaller, it explodes: pop and keep fighting.
Equal sizes: pop the top and the current one dies too.
If the current asteroid survives, push it.
pitfalls: Treating `[-2, 2]` as a collision; they move apart.
Using an ArrayList and removing from the middle is O(n²).

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
summary: Find the largest rectangle under a histogram. Keep a stack of bar indices with increasing heights. When a shorter bar arrives, each taller bar popped can extend no further right; its width runs from the new stack top + 1 to the current index − 1.

complexity.note: Each bar is pushed and popped once.

intuition: For each bar, the best rectangle using its full height stretches until a shorter bar on each side.
An increasing stack gives the left boundary (the element below it) for free.
The bar that pops it is the right boundary.
A sentinel height 0 at the end flushes the stack.
pitfalls: Computing width as `i - popped` instead of `i - stack.peek() - 1`.
Forgetting to flush the stack at the end.
O(n²) expansion from each bar times out.

Python.code:
def largestRectangleArea(heights: List[int]) -> int:
    stack = []
    best, n = 0, len(heights)
    for i in range(n + 1):
        h = 0 if i == n else heights[i]
        while stack and heights[stack[-1]] > h:
            height = heights[stack.pop()]
            left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
            width = i - left - 1
            best = max(best, height * width)
        stack.append(i)
    return best
